title: How a bioceramic sealer sets
topic: Premixed calcium-silicate sealers set with water drawn from dentin, leach Ca²⁺/OH⁻, and in vitro grow apatite-like mineral at the wall.

claims.claim: Premixed sealer: water from the dentin soaks in; a very dry canal may stay unset
claims.source: Xuereb et al., J Endod 2015;41:111–124 (PMID 25442723); Antunes et al., Aust Endod J 2026;52:168–177 (PMID 41364608)

claims.claim: Silicate grains hydrate: C₃S/C₂S + H₂O → C–S–H gel + Ca(OH)₂ (simplified)
Hydration takes hours–days; premixed sealer final set ≥168 h (Gilmore)
Ca²⁺ and OH⁻ leach out; pH ~10–12 in lab tests (water)
claims.source: Lee et al., Bioinorg Chem Appl 2017;2017:2582849 (PMID 28210204) for pH (Table 5, distilled water); Ca²⁺ release: Candeiro et al., J Endod 2012;38:842–845 (PMID 22595123); Xuereb et al., J Endod 2015;41:111–124 (PMID 25442723)

claims.claim: Steps overlap: pH rises within minutes, before setting
claims.source: Lee et al., Bioinorg Chem Appl 2017;2017:2582849 (PMID 28210204), Table 5: pH 11.64 at 3 min

claims.claim: Phosphate from tissue fluid reaches the sealer up the tubules (lab: PBS bath)
claims.source: Toy model / schematic: route is illustrative; in the cited studies specimens were immersed in PBS (Han & Okiji 2013)

claims.claim: Phosphate + Ca²⁺ → apatite-like layer and tag-like Ca–P deposits in tubules (days–months, lab)
claims.source: Han & Okiji, Int Endod J 2013;46:808–814 (PMID 23402321); Xuereb et al., J Endod 2015;41:111–124 (PMID 25442723); MTA: Sarkar et al., J Endod 2005;31:97–100 (PMID 15671817)

claims.claim: Water sets it. In vitro, calcium + phosphate form apatite-like mineral
claims.source: Donnermeyer et al., Odontology 2019;107:421–436 (PMID 30554288); apatite-like (acicular Ca–P precipitates, Ca/P 1.6–2.0, in PBS): Han & Okiji, Int Endod J 2013;46:808–814 (PMID 23402321)

claims.claim: Premixed sealers can take days to set and need dentin moisture
claims.source: Loushine et al., J Endod 2011;37:673–677 (PMID 21496669); Xuereb et al., J Endod 2015;41:111–124 (PMID 25442723). End-card source lines: Loushine 2011 J Endod · Xuereb 2015 J Endod / Han & Okiji 2013 IEJ · Donnermeyer 2019 Odontology

claims.claim: Ion release = some solubility; long-term seal effect debated

caption:
How does a premixed bioceramic sealer set?
Premixed calcium-silicate sealers carry no water: they hydrate with dentin moisture, so a very dry canal can delay the set.
Hydration forms C–S–H gel + Ca(OH)₂; Ca²⁺ and OH⁻ leach out and pH reaches ~10–12 in lab tests.
In PBS, calcium + phosphate form apatite-like deposits at the wall and in tubules. In vitro only: clinical bioactivity is unproven, and ion release means some solubility.
Refs: Xuereb 2015, J Endod; Antunes 2026, Aust Endod J; Camilleri 2011, Dent Mater; Loushine 2011, J Endod; Lee 2017, Bioinorg Chem Appl; Han & Okiji 2013, IEJ; Sarkar 2005, J Endod (MTA); Donnermeyer 2019, Odontology.
